rawFindings.title: Empty file patterns are expanded to a filesystem-root glob
rawFindings.explanation: Mapping every pattern without first removing empty strings means an empty pattern is passed to `processPath()`. Since `path.resolve(cwd, "")` is the current working directory and is a directory, `processPath()` converts the empty pattern to `/**/*.js` (or the configured extension glob), causing later globbing to search from the filesystem root instead of ignoring the empty argument.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore filtering of empty patterns before mapping, e.g. `return patterns.filter(p => p.length).map(processPathExtensions);`.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Calling `resolveFileGlobPatterns([""], { cwd: "/tmp/project" })` now returns `["/**/*.js"]`; `executeOnFiles([""])` can then lint matching `.js` files outside `/tmp/project` rather than processing no files.
